description: One node in a scene file: add, read, set, duplicate, reparent or delete it, or paint TileMap cells. Any ClassDB node type can be added, so a NavigationRegion2D, an AnimationTree or a Camera3D is an add with that nodeType and its properties, and another scene is instanced by an add with instancePath. A set with properties {"name": "Boss"} renames a node. A property holding a Resource takes the res:// path of one, so a texture, a material or a theme is a set like any other. A write is refused while the editor holds unsaved changes to the scene, and for a node that belongs to a scene this one instances or inherits. Through the editor when one serves the project; with none, a headless engine runs the editor's own tool and the answer says so under writtenBy, or readBy for a read. That engine runs every script of the file, where the editor runs only tool scripts, so what a script changes as the file loads or as a property is set is put back before anything is saved, and a file where that cannot be done, such as a scene whose script does not compile, is refused and nothing is written. An editor of the project that is running and has not reached this server is waited for rather than written around. Operations: add (needs nodeName): add a node of any class, or an instance of a scene; get (needs nodePath): read a node's properties, and a TileMapLayer's or TileMap's cells as set_tilemap_cells takes them, the first 1000 with cellCount for all; set (needs nodePath, properties): set properties on a node; duplicate (needs nodePath, newName): copy a node and its children; reparent (needs nodePath, newParentPath): move a node under another parent, or to another place among its siblings; delete (needs nodePath): remove a node and its children; set_tilemap_cells (needs nodePath, cells): place tiles in a TileMapLayer or TileMap.

cells.description: Cells to place. Only for op set_tilemap_cells.

includeDefaults.description: get: include properties still at their default. Default false. Only for op get.

index.description: add and reparent: where the node goes among the parent's children, 0 for first. Default last. Child order is draw order in a CanvasItem and layout order in a Container. Only for ops add, reparent.

instancePath.description: add: a scene to instance as the new node instead of a class, such as "ui/panel.tscn". It is saved as an instance of that file, the way the editor's Instantiate Child Scene saves one, so changes to that scene reach it; properties set its root. A scene that is the target or instances it is refused. Only for op add.

layer.description: set_tilemap_cells: the layer of a TileMap. Default 0. A TileMapLayer is one layer. Only for op set_tilemap_cells.

newName.description: duplicate: the copy's name. Only for op duplicate.

newParentPath.description: reparent: the new parent, which may be the one it has, to move it among its siblings. Only for op reparent.

nodeName.description: add: the new node's name. Only for op add.

nodePath.description: Node path from the scene root, such as "Player/Sprite2D". "." is the root. Only for ops get, set, duplicate, reparent, delete, set_tilemap_cells.

nodeType.description: add: the node class, such as "CharacterBody2D". Give this or instancePath. Only for op add.

parentNodePath.description: add: where the node goes. Default the root. duplicate: where the copy goes. Only for ops add, duplicate.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the project directory, the one holding project.godot.

properties.description: Properties to set, keyed by Godot property name. Vectors, colours and the like may be written as {"x": 1, "y": 2} or tagged {"_type": "Vector2", "x": 1, "y": 2}, which is the form a read answers with, so a value read off one node can be written straight to another. A key may also be a colon path into one of the components of a vector, a colour, a rectangle or a transform, as GDScript names them, so one axis is written alone: "position:x", "modulate:a", "region_rect:size:y"; a component the value does not have is refused, naming the ones it has. A property holding a node takes the path to it from the node being set, such as "../Player". Each value is read back once set, and one the engine changed or refused is refused with what it holds. A whole number of 2^53 or more, such as a 64-bit seed or a resource uid, is written as its digits, {"_type": "int", "value": "9007199254740993"}, the form a read answers with: a JSON number that large can arrive as a neighbour of the one sent, so sent as a number it is refused. Only for ops add, set.

scenePath.description: Scene file inside the project, such as "scenes/main.tscn" or "res://scenes/main.tscn".

name: scene_node
title: Scene nodes
